title: Checking Python Version and Runtime Environment
description: Import sys, platform, and subprocess, define _sh(cmd), and print sys.version.split()[0], platform.platform(), and whether google.colab is loaded.

steps.description: Import `sys`, `platform`, and `subprocess` and define `_sh(cmd)` to run a shell command with `subprocess.check_output` inside a `try/except` block.
Print the short Python version `sys.version.split()[0]`, the OS string `platform.platform()`, and the boolean `"google.colab" in sys.modules`.

Look at line 9 (`sys.version.split()[0]`): splitting the full `sys.version` string on whitespace and taking index `0` extracts just the version number (`3.12.16`) without the build date and compiler info.

steps.question: What does `sys.version.split()[0]` on line 9 return compared to `sys.version`, and what does line 11 print when `google.colab` is not imported?
steps.answer: `sys.version.split()[0]` returns just the version token (`3.12.16`), and line 11 prints `In Colab: False`.

steps.description: Line 11 evaluates `"google.colab" in sys.modules` and prints `In Colab: False`.
